name: DFRobot DFR0998 Fermion: SD3031 precision RTC breakout (I2C real time clock, CR1220 backup)
//: Catalog record written by /spark:research on 2026-09-29 — read, not chosen. Filled ONLY from what was actually read: DFRobot's wiki and product page, and the schematic PDF the wiki links (rendered and read as an image; it has no text layer). A null is a fact nobody has recorded. verified: true = the vendor's own text at the cited URL; read off an image, inferred or computed = false with why_it_matters.
//why_not: Cheapest of DFRobot's RTCs ($4.90) and the only one with 4.7 k pull-ups, but it is 3.3 V only and rated -10 to +70 °C — too narrow for an unheated garden box, when the DS3231-family boards cost a few dollars more and are rated to -40 °C.
also_known_as: Fermion: SD3031 Precision RTC Module for Arduino (Breakout)
//variant: True of the DFR0998 at schematic V1.0 dated 2022-10-31 (the PDF is titled '[DFR0998][M027.00775](V1.0.0)'). Same 22.5 x 21 mm outline and seven-pad row as the DS3231-family Fermion boards, but pad 6 is NC here where they have RST, the chip is Wave's SD3031 at address 0x32 instead of 0x68, and the pull-ups differ.
//sources: The wiki links no dimension drawing and no datasheet for this board — only the schematic and the library. The library https://github.com/DFRobot/DFRobot_SD3031 is linked from the wiki and was NOT opened.

needs.note: Pulled to the module's VCC by R2 4.7k on the module (schematic image).
Pulled to the module's VCC by R1 4.7k on the module (schematic image).
'Active-low interrupt or 1Hz square wave output' (wiki). Pulled to VCC by R3 10k on the module (schematic image).

power.note: 'Supply Voltage: 3.3V' — DFRobot give a single value, not a range. The pull-ups return to this pin, so it also sets the bus's high level.

unused_pins.note: Pad 6 is 'NC' on the wiki table and on the schematic's P1 — the position the DS3231-family Fermion boards use for RST.
'32.768KHz pulse output' (wiki); the schematic image shows it pulled to VCC by R4 10k from the chip's F32K pin.

//pin_order: Seven pads, numbered 1..7 on the wiki's table and on the schematic's P1: VCC GND SCL SDA INT NC 32K. Which physical end is pad 1 is not known — there is no dimension drawing and nothing was measured.

body_mm.where: 'Dimension: 22.5×21mm/0.89×0.83"' — vendor text; no drawing is published, so hole and header positions are unknown
body_mm.why_it_matters: every placement is arranged around it

i2c_address.where: Specification: 'I2C Address: 0x32' (the wiki prints it as '0×32')

supply_v.where: 'Supply Voltage: 3.3V' — a single value, not a range
supply_v.why_it_matters: Not a 5 V part; fine for the FireBeetle's 3.3 V logic and nothing else.

timekeeping_accuracy_ppm.where: 'Timing Accuracy: ±3.8ppm @ 25℃' — at 25 °C only; no figure over temperature is given

operating_temperature_c.why_it_matters: The reason it was passed over: a garden box in a Czech winter goes below -10 °C.

backup_cell.where: product page: CR1220 coin cell, not rechargeable, not included ('does not come with batteries')

timekeeping_battery_current_ua.where: '1.8µA when powered by button cell battery'

module_has_i2c_pullups.where: read off the schematic IMAGE (the PDF has no text layer): R1 4.7k SCL to VCC, R2 4.7k SDA to VCC
module_has_i2c_pullups.why_it_matters: The FireBeetle 2 ESP32-S3 V1.2+ has no I2C pull-ups of its own, so whether the module brings them decides whether the bus has any.

i2c_pullup_ohms.where: R1, R2 = 4.7k on the schematic image
i2c_pullup_ohms.why_it_matters: 4.7k is the usual value and supports 400 kHz with more bus capacitance than the DS3231-family boards' 10k; it also sinks 0.7 mA per line when low.

int_pullup_ohms.where: R3 10k, INT to VCC, on the schematic image
int_pullup_ohms.why_it_matters: What an interrupt or wake input sees; no host pull-up is needed.

cell_holder_on_board.where: BT1 on VBAT on the schematic image, and the product page names the CR1220; no photo or drawing was read
cell_holder_on_board.why_it_matters: The 'own backup cell' is this holder plus a cell you buy.

cell_charged_by_module.where: on the schematic image VBAT connects to BT1, C1 100nF and chip pin 6 only — no diode or resistor from VCC
cell_charged_by_module.why_it_matters: Fit a primary CR1220, as the product page says; a rechargeable cell would not be charged.

host_requirements: Feed VCC with 3.3 V only — DFRobot state a single supply value — and from the logic rail, since the module's pull-ups return to VCC.
Add no I2C pull-ups; the module brings 4.7k on each line.
Not for an installation that sees below -10 °C or above +70 °C.

sourcing.stock: not stated on the page; ships without the CR1220
